clue.text: Lead sheep in newly formed company

parts.note: the lead in a film or play is its star
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A shepherd leads a ram into a flock that has only just been assembled.
explanation.definitionFit: A start-up is the usual business term for a young company just launched.

clue.text: Article to cover extremity in strike

definitions.meaning: an item of clothing worn over the foot
to hit someone hard with the fist

explanation.surface: Clothing for the feet worn on a picket line.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a garment for the foot and a slang word for a punch.

clue.text: Four internally occupying large capsule

indicators.note: the inner letters occupy the large word, sitting inside it

parts.note: ample means large

indicators.note: internally means the interior letters, without the ends

explanation.surface: Four tablets taken internally from a big container.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampoule is a small sealed glass capsule holding a dose of a drug.

clue.text: Rot in time fully developed

parts.note: ripe fruit is fully developed

explanation.surface: Fruit goes bad once it has had time to mature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot' looks like decay, matching the surface; it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is slang for nonsense or rubbish, as rot is.

clue.text: Place line about rising nation in advertisement for drama

indicators.note: about means around, so these letters surround the nation

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: Libya is a North African nation

explanation.surface: A poster for a play put up about a country's uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: A playbill is a poster announcing a theatrical production.

clue.text: Attack persistently dismal crowd in retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the letters of both words are read from the end

parts.note: dismal means drab
a mob is a crowd

explanation.surface: A miserable mob, pulling back, keeps up its assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' reverses both words together, so the crowd's letters end up first.
explanation.definitionFit: To bombard is to assail continually, as with shells or questions.

clue.text: Poet in past lacking focused vision

indicators.note: in places the poet inside the past word

parts.note: by means past, as in time went by
Edward Lear was a nonsense poet

explanation.surface: A poet of former times who could not see clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleary eyes are dim and blurred, unable to see sharply.

clue.text: Preserve a medal thrown out after damage

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the damage word

parts.note: to mar is to damage

indicators.note: thrown out suggests being cast into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Keeping a medal that was discarded after being harmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserve' looks like a verb; it is the noun for jam.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is a citrus fruit preserve spread on toast.

clue.text: Expression of surprise about retreat after a suspension of law

indicators.note: after places the enclosed piece following the single letter
about means around, so the surprise word encloses the retreat

parts.note: my! is an exclamation of surprise
a nest is a cosy retreat

explanation.surface: Gasps greet a withdrawal following a halt to legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is a pardon, a waiving of legal penalties for a period.

clue.text: Wanted things in agreement endlessly disrupted by party traitor

indicators.note: being disrupted means broken into, so the other letters go inside
endlessly means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a deal is an agreement
a side is a party in a dispute
a rat is a traitor

explanation.surface: A pact everyone wanted is wrecked by a turncoat in one faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts DEAL to DEA, which SIDERAT then splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderata are things needed or desired, from the Latin for things longed for.

clue.text: Delight in top bond, having tax covered

parts.note: a cap is a top, as on a bottle

indicators.note: having the tax covered means the bond word goes round it

parts.note: a tie is a bond
VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled with a premium bond whose tax liability is taken care of.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate is to charm or enchant, a verb synonym of delight.

clue.text: Marks that are made round extracts in speech

indicators.note: in speech signals that a word is spoken, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: wrings, as in wrings a confession out of someone, means extracts

explanation.surface: Annotations drawn as circles around quoted passages from an address.
explanation.walkthrough: The W of WRINGS is silent, so it is heard the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Circular marks, such as those left by a wet glass, are rings.

clue.text: Choice of food returned by idiot breaking taboo without shame

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a menu offers a choice of food

indicators.note: the idiot breaks into the taboo word, splitting it

parts.note: something taboo is barred, forbidden
an ass is an idiot

explanation.surface: A fool sends back his dinner order and flouts a prohibition, quite unabashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unembarrassed means feeling no awkwardness or shame, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Fiasco admitted by king, for example, raised in conflict with official line

indicators.note: admitted by means let in, so the king word holds the fiasco

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia
a mess is a fiasco

indicators.note: in a down entry raised means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A monarch owns up to a blunder, raised as an example of dissent from policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns EG into GE. Offa built Offa's Dyke on the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: A politician off-message departs from the agreed party line.

clue.text: Bank wholly behind start of financial decline that's unstoppable

indicators.note: placed behind means coming after the first piece
the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a reef is a bank of rock or sand under the sea
wholly means all

explanation.surface: An entire bank backs the launch of a financial collapse nobody can halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A free fall is a sudden uncontrolled drop, used of prices or markets plummeting.

clue.text: Sporting body with change of law ends time of illusory promise

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association, which governs English football

indicators.note: a change of letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sports governing body changes its rules, ending a hopeful era.
explanation.definitionFit: A false dawn is an apparent improvement that comes to nothing, a deceptive beginning.

clue.text: Brief film, gripping western

indicators.note: gripping means holding inside, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a film is a thin layer

explanation.surface: A short movie that grabs hold of a cowboy picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' looks like an adjective about the film; it is the noun for a barrister or solicitor.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a brief is a lawyer, especially one defending in court.

clue.text: Gloomy individual, embraced by dame, cheers up

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the dame letters go round

parts.note: DBE is Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire, an honour that makes a woman a dame
own means individual, belonging to oneself

indicators.note: in a down entry up means read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A miserable person is hugged by a grande dame and perks up.
explanation.definitionFit: Downbeat means pessimistic or low in mood, synonymous with gloomy.

clue.text: Might head of convent left inside meditate?

indicators.note: inside puts these letters within the meditate word

parts.note: to muse is to meditate

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A question about whether a mother superior, abandoned, should reflect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb; it is the noun for strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means physical strength or power, as might does.

clue.text: Sons quarrelled less following betrayal

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son or sons

indicators.note: less means without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: fell out means quarrelled
F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

explanation.surface: Brothers fought less after one of them was betrayed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sell-out is a betrayal of principles or allies for gain.

clue.text: Firm with load of mineral around tip

indicators.note: with here means holding within, so the firm word contains the rest

parts.note: firm means fast, as in fixed fast
ore is a load of mineral dug from a mine
C stands for circa, Latin for around

explanation.surface: A mining company with a heap of rock round a spoil tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' suggests a slag heap; it is a prediction, as in a racing tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is a prediction of an outcome, so a forecast is a synonym.

clue.text: Climbing mountain, carrier of information about us moving slowly

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means read upwards, so both words are backwards

parts.note: Etna is a volcanic mountain in Sicily
DNA carries our genetic information

explanation.surface: Climbers on a mountain carry news of their slow progress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climbing' reverses both pieces as one run, so the information carrier ends up first; 'about us' is part of its description.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is a musical direction for a moderately slow, walking tempo.

clue.text: Greatest mass taken in by touts in chaos

indicators.note: taken in means held inside, so the mass letter goes within
in chaos means in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge crowd is conned by ticket touts amid pandemonium.
explanation.definitionFit: Utmost means greatest or most extreme, as in of the utmost importance.

clue.text: Urgent devil, so deviously persuasive

indicators.note: deviously means in a twisted, roundabout way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pressing demon cunningly talks people round.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver-tongued describes someone eloquent and able to win people over.

clue.text: President wanting vote to support acceptable alliance

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits below the other

parts.note: U means upper-class and so socially acceptable

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: Richard Nixon was a US president
X is the mark made on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A president needing votes backs an agreeable coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining together, a league or alliance.

clue.text: Width of character in complete illustration

indicators.note: in places the printer's measure inside the complete word

parts.note: to do a task is to complete it
an em is a printing measure, the width of a letter M

explanation.surface: A typesetter measures each letter in a finished picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A demo is a demonstration, a practical illustration of how something works.

clue.text: Bouquet in course of drama romantically presented

indicators.note: the letters lie within the run of the following words

explanation.surface: A bunch of flowers features in a romantic stage play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bouquet' suggests flowers; here it is the smell of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its characteristic scent or fragrance.

clue.text: When guarding base, that is dutiful behaviour

indicators.note: guarding means surrounding protectively, so one word goes round the others

parts.note: once means when, as in once you arrive
a bed is a base, as in a bed of concrete
i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: Behaving as duty requires while protecting a military base.
explanation.definitionFit: Obedience is compliance with orders, the conduct of the dutiful.

clue.text: Variable element in religious group missing leader no longer around

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the shortened group
missing its leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a sect is a religious group
X is the classic algebra variable
tin is a chemical element

explanation.surface: A leaderless cult with an unstable member has died out.
explanation.definitionFit: Something extinct has died out completely and survives nowhere now.

clue.text: Set nothing next to brown fruit

indicators.note: next to places the first two pieces beside the brown word, after it

parts.note: tan is a light brown
to gel is to set, like jelly
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A cook sets aside nothing beside a browned fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus hybrid of tangerine and pomelo or grapefruit.
